analysis.title: US Equity Positioning Update: Volatility Reprices Higher Ahead of Midterms
key_insights: Hedge funds cut risk aggressively last week, with most of the reduction on Wednesday and Thursday before Friday's sell-off. It was the third largest degross week YTD. Long reductions and added shorts dropped net exposure to the 10th percentile on a 5-year lookback.
Semis net exposure fell the most over October and is back to the July lows. All sectors saw risk taken down.
Hyperscaler exposure swung widely during the week and nets finished near local lows. The group is still one of the largest net length pockets for the AI trade.
Short exposure in Industrials, Financials, Healthcare and Communication Services is at or near 5-year highs.
Composite positioning moved further underweight, driven by large reductions from Balanced and Value funds.

Risk Control funds sold an estimated $160bn of equities over two days, cutting exposure to the 65th percentile from the 93rd percentile the prior week. Their sensitivity to volatility also fell, but they are still expected to sell about $105-120bn of equity risk on another -2% day.
CTA global equity exposure is in the 9th percentile after hitting various sell triggers on Friday.
Levered and Inverse ETFs sold $30bn of equity risk on Friday's move. Their exposure is now below median levels.
Index and single-name implied volatility repriced higher, with VIX and VIXEQ closing at their highest levels since July. Skew rose sharply, which suggests clients moved quickly to hedge.
The US midterm elections are pricing the largest one-day SPX breakeven move through year-end, at just over 1%.
Corporates are quiet and not buying back stock.

sector_views.rationale: Semis saw the largest net exposure decline in October among hedge funds, back to July lows. This is a positioning observation, not a rating.
Hedge fund short exposure in these sectors is at or near 5-year highs. This describes positioning, not a UBS rating.

risk_factors: Risk Control funds have further selling capacity if the market has another -2% day.
US midterm elections create event risk, with the largest one-day breakeven move through year-end priced at just over 1% for the SPX.
Hedge fund nets are near lows and shorts in several sectors are at 5-year highs, which leaves positioning stretched.
